nanojs.title: NanoJS
nanojs.tagline: A lightweight JavaScript runtime and bytecode interpreter I built from scratch in C++ to see how JS actually works under the hood.

stats.label: Custom Engine
stats.detail: Hand-written lexer, parser, and stack VM

nanojs.heading: Why Build Another JavaScript Runtime?
nanojs.problemText: Most of us write JavaScript every single day, but huge runtimes like Node and V8 feel like black boxes full of complex C++ abstractions.
nanojs.solutionText: I wanted to understand everything from the ground up: how raw source text turns into tokens, how the AST is walked, how bytecode instructions get generated, and how a stack-based virtual machine evaluates them.

highlights.title: Hand-Rolled Lexer & Recursive Descent Parser
highlights.desc: Tokenizes input and builds an abstract syntax tree without leaning on external parser generators like Lex or Yacc.

highlights.title: Bytecode Compiler & Virtual Machine
highlights.desc: Flattens the AST into a compact bytecode stream and executes operations with a simple, high-speed stack VM.

highlights.title: Custom Object & Memory Model
highlights.desc: Implements basic prototype lookups, numbers, strings, and closures with manual memory management.

steps.title: Lexing & Tokenizing
steps.desc: Converts plain JS code strings into typed tokens while keeping line and column numbers for friendly errors.

steps.title: AST Compilation
steps.desc: Parses grammar rules, handles operator precedence, and spits out clean bytecode instructions.

steps.title: Stack VM Execution
steps.desc: The virtual machine runs the opcodes in a tight loop, managing call frames and the evaluation stack.

nanojs.takeaway: Building a runtime from scratch completely demystified language internals and made me a way sharper systems and full-stack programmer.

stats.label: Ingestion Latency

orbitform.heading: Stop Building Form Backends From Scratch
orbitform.problemText: Every time you build a landing page, portfolio, or client site, you have to write another API route, wire up an email service, set up spam checks, and deal with broken CORS headers.
orbitform.solutionText: OrbitForm solves this in one line: point your form's action attribute to your unique OrbitForm endpoint, and you get automatic honeypot bot blocking, clean email notifications, and webhooks that ping Slack or Discord instantly.

highlights.title: Plug-and-Play Endpoints
highlights.desc: Works with plain HTML, React, Next.js, Webflow, or Framer with zero SDKs or client libraries required.

highlights.title: Built-In Spam & Honeypot Filtering
highlights.desc: Catches bot submissions invisibly without annoying real visitors with slow Captchas.

highlights.title: Instant Integrations & Webhooks
highlights.desc: Forwards leads straight into Telegram, Discord, Slack, or any custom API with retry support.

steps.title: Create Your Endpoint
steps.desc: Sign in and grab your unique form endpoint URL in about 10 seconds.

steps.title: Paste Into Your HTML
steps.desc: Set <form action="https://orbitform.space/f/..." method="POST"> on your site.

steps.title: Receive Submissions
steps.desc: Get notified immediately via email or webhook whenever someone fills out your form.

orbitform.takeaway: Built as a personal productivity tool to kill repetitive backend work, now helping developers launch landing pages much faster.
